summary: Unexpected routing to cold/slow model variant causing elevated latency and request timeouts for customer NovaHealth
description:
Issue summary:
Customer NovaHealth reported a sudden increase in inference latency (p90 jumping from ~120ms to 2.5s) and intermittent request timeouts for chat completions between 2026-03-09T18:00Z and 2026-03-10T03:00Z. They observed a correlation with our fallback routing events where requests were routed to what appears to be a slower model variant (apparently cold or not warmed on Dedicated pool).

Impact:
- Multiple customer API requests returned 504/timeouts and streaming sessions dropped after ~10s.
- Overall p95/p99 latency elevated causing partial degradation of NovaHealth's production feature.
- Customer on Dedicated plan; expects reserved performance SLAs.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: dp-novahealth-us-east-1 (GPU A100 clusters)
- API: hosted endpoint (redwood.api.com) invoking model redwood/gpt-3.8-optimized with fallback variants available
- Observed regions: us-east-1

Steps to reproduce (as observed by customer):
1) Send concurrent chat.complete requests at 30 req/s to their pinned endpoint (model pinned to redwood/gpt-3.8-optimized with routing fallback enabled).
2) ~15-25% of requests receive a slow response (1.5s-4.0s).
3) ~5% of requests fail with 504 timeout after 10s.
4) Traces show routing decision to a variant with suffix "-vcold" or to a quantized 8-bit variant with spin-up logs.

Observed logs / metrics snippets:
- routing.log: "route_decision: fallback -> redwood/gpt-3.8-optimized-vcold (reason: capacity-constrained, policy: latency_cost_balance)"
- scheduler: "pod_start: model=redwood/gpt-3.8-optimized-vcold node=gpu-12 boot_time=62s"
- ingress: spike in 5xx at 2026-03-09T21:12Z correlating with fallback events
- console traces: KV cache miss rates increased by 35% for affected routes

Initial hypothesis:
- Fallback policy kicked in due to temporary capacity pressure. The fallback target was a variant that was not warmed (cold-start) resulting in high start-up latency.
- Alternatively, a routing config change inadvertently included a slower quantized variant in the fallback list for this customer's route.
- Autoscaler delay or pre-warming disabled for certain fallout variants in the dedicated pool.

Investigation notes (SRE/Support):
- Confirmed several routing decisions to "-vcold" variants in routing logs between 2026-03-09T20:50Z and 2026-03-10T02:10Z.
- Pod start times for those variants averaged 55-70s (consistent with observed 504s when requests queued).
- Dedicated autoscaling metrics show CPU/GPU utilization at 78% but burst queueing occurred when many new variant pods needed initialization.
- Reviewed rollout policies: customer endpoint had "allow_fallback=true" and policy "latency_cost_balance" which permits switching to cheaper/quantized variants under pressure.
- No recent code deploys to routing in the 48h before the incident; a config change to routing policies was made by infra on 2026-03-08 (INT-1182) to add additional fallback targets cluster-wide.

Temporary mitigations applied:
- Support requested an immediate override: set allow_fallback=false on NovaHealth endpoint to force routing to pinned model only (applied 2026-03-10T02:40Z).
- SRE increased pre-warm counts for the dedicated pool as a stopgap to reduce cold starts for common variants.
- Enabled conservative autoscaler thresholds for dp-novahealth-us-east-1 for 24h window.

Next steps / action items:
- [SRE] Revert cluster-wide routing fallback addition or scope it to self_serve customers (INT-1182 follow-up). Target: 2026-03-13.
- [Platform] Add warm pool/pre-warm config per fallback variant to avoid cold-starts for Dedicated customers. ETA: design 2026-03-17.
- [Support] Communicate detailed incident summary to NovaHealth with RCA and timeline. Owner: Aisha Khan. ETA: 2026-03-12.
- [Engineering] Add telemetry to routing decisions to record "variant_warm_state" and pod_boot_time in trace context. ETA: 2026-03-20.

Customer-impact resolution status:
- After allow_fallback=false was applied, latency returned to pre-incident baselines and timeouts stopped. Customer confirmed reduced error rates in their environment on 2026-03-10.

Notes:
- Need to balance cost-aware fallback policies with SLA expectations for Dedicated/Enterprise customers. Consider automatic policy override for dedicated tiers.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Configure endpoint with allow_fallback=true and latency_cost_balance policy on a dedicated pool. 2) Generate a burst of requests to saturate dedicated pool capacity. 3) Observe routing decisions in routing.log and watch for pod_start events indicating cold-start. 4) Measure p95 latency and timeout rate.
comments: 2026-03-10 03:05 - Marcus Reed (SRE): Confirmed routing logs show fallback to -vcold variants. Autoscaler did not pre-warm due to conservative policy. Attaching trace IDs in related_github_prs.
2026-03-10 08:22 - Elena Park (Platform): We rolled the routing change in INT-1182 to add additional fallback variants. Narrowing scope looks like the right short-term fix for Dedicated pools.
2026-03-10 11:47 - Aisha Khan (Support): Customer confirmed errors returned to baseline after allow_fallback=false. Preparing communication and refund calculation for affected window.
2026-03-11 09:12 - Product (Diego Morales): Proposal: auto-disable cost-based fallback for endpoints tagged dedicated/enterprise. Will draft RFC.
resolution: Mitigated by overriding allow_fallback on the customer's endpoint and increasing pre-warm counts. Working on longer-term fix to avoid routing to cold variants for Dedicated tiers.
